items.caption: A modern redraw of 包 in Shuowen seal-script style. Shuowen interpreted the received form as pregnancy, with the inner shape representing an unformed child; the image does not establish that interpretation as the graph’s origin.
items.alt: A black seal-script-style form with an inner curved stroke enclosed by a larger outer stroke that extends above and below, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: This redraw shows the received form associated with Shuowen’s pregnancy interpretation. It is useful for illustrating that interpretation, while its modern origin and the graph’s unresolved history are made clear.

limitations.text: This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image. Shuowen’s pregnancy interpretation and the proposal that 包 developed from a graph depicting someone holding a child are competing accounts; the earliest form and any sequence connecting them remain unresolved.
The sources record pregnancy and wrapping as separate interpretations or uses but do not establish whether one sense developed from the other.
